name: spotnote-mcp

tools.name: watch_notes
tools.description: Wait for notes that need you: new notes, and developer replies on notes you asked about or resolved. Returns them in a batch, or nothing after the timeout. Answer each note it returns with resolve_note, dismiss_note or reply_note (resolve it if nothing needs changing), then call it again to keep working hands-free.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait. Default and max 50.

tools.name: list_notes
tools.description: List all open notes, including ones watch_notes already returned. Each note's prompt names the exact source file, line and column of the element.

tools.name: reply_note
tools.description: Write to the developer on a note: a question when the request is unclear, or why you won't make the change. They see it on the note in the browser; their answer comes back through watch_notes.

message.description: What to tell or ask the developer. Short Markdown: a paragraph or two, or a list; `code`; files as path:line.

tools.name: dismiss_note
tools.description: Close a note without making the change, when you shouldn't or can't (it's out of scope, already done, or would break something). The developer sees your reason; if they reply, the note comes back through watch_notes. To ask something instead, use reply_note.

reason.description: Why you won't make the change. One or two sentences, Markdown.

tools.name: resolve_note
tools.description: Mark a note done after you've made the change, or answered its question. The developer sees a check mark on its pin and your summary on the note. If they reply that it isn't right, the note comes back through watch_notes.

summary.description: Markdown: what you changed, and in which file (path:line); or, for a question, the answer.

instructions: Spotnote notes are requests the developer writes on UI elements of their running app, in the browser. Each note names the exact source file, line and column. To work through them hands-free, call watch_notes in a loop: handle what it returns, then call it again. A wait that ends with nothing is normal: keep watching until the developer tells you to stop. The developer is looking at the browser, not at this chat: ask questions with reply_note (they answer in the browser and the answer comes back through watch_notes). End every note you get with resolve_note, dismiss_note or reply_note, even when there's nothing to change. A note can be a question ("what does this do?"): answer it in resolve_note's summary. If the developer only says thanks or confirms, resolve it with a word or two. Messages show as Markdown in a narrow panel: keep them short, split points into paragraphs or a "- " list, put code and props in `backticks`, and write files as path:line (the developer can click them to open the file).
